newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon sets security limits on "hunger revolt".
newsitem.headline: Lebanon sets security limits on "hunger revolt".

text.p: Lebanon's interior minister said on Wednesday the government would allow residents of the eastern Bekaa Valley to take part in a "hunger revolt" but warned that the armed forces would not tolerate acts that threaten security.
"The state will not fight the citizens and will not suppress the protesters. But with respect to violating general security, this is not allowed," minister Michel al-Murr said.
"Security elements will not allow any security violations or harm to security institutions or other public institutions," he was quoted by the official National News Agency as saying.

Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili, who led the pro-Iranian Hizbollah in the 1980s, is urging Bekaa residents to start a "hunger revolt" on July 4 to pressure the Beirut government into easing poverty in the region which is suffering economically from a crackdown on illegal drug crops.
He has threatened to lead a march on Beirut if civil disobedience measures -- refusing to pay taxes and utilities fees -- fail to persuade the government to meet his demands.
Tufaili has called on Bekaa residents to gather in the town of Baalbek -- a Hizbollah stronghold -- to launch the civil disobedience campaign.
"The (July 4) gathering is accepted on condition that it does not lead to clashes with security forces," al-Murr said

Tufaili's civil disobedience call has alarmed the authorities in Beirut. President Elias Hrawi has threated the radical Shi'ite Moslem cleric with legal action and accused his supporters of threatening Lebanon with a return to chaos.

The Lebanese government last month allocated 150 billion pounds ($97 million) to develop the Bekaa. Beirut newspapers implied that the decision was designed to take the steam out of Tufaili's campaign.
Tufaili's campaign has captured headlines on the front pages of Lebanese newspapers and triggered debate in recent weeks.
The cleric has insisted the "hunger revolt" will go ahead as planned on Friday.
